title: Add tests for Database CRUD operations (app/storage/db.py)
body:
## Summary

The `Database` class in `app/storage/db.py` has 18 methods covering CRUD operations for sources, transcripts, summaries, reports, and tags — but none of them have Python-level tests. Only raw SQL schema tests exist in `tests/test_schema.py`.

## Scope

- Write a test suite in `tests/test_db.py` that covers all public methods of the `Database` class.
- Use the existing `tmp_db_path` fixture from `conftest.py` (which creates a temp SQLite DB).
- Stub out or mock the `Database._conn()` method to use the temp DB path.
- Test at least:
  - `insert_source`, `get_source`, `list_sources`, `update_source_status`, `count_sources`, `get_source_by_url`
  - `insert_transcript`, `get_transcript`
  - `insert_summary`, `get_source_summaries`, `get_source_summary_count`, `get_summaries_in_week`
  - `insert_report`, `list_reports`, `get_report`
  - `ensure_tag`, `add_source_tag`, `get_source_tags`
  - `add_report_source`
  - `clear_all_tables`
- Each test should create a `Database` instance, perform operations, and assert on the return values.
- Follow the style of existing tests (plain `assert`, descriptive function names).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 18+ public methods have at least one test
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_db.py -v` passes
- [ ] No external dependencies (DB file is temporary, cleaned up after test)
- [ ] Tests are isolated — no shared state between them

## Getting Started

- Read `app/storage/db.py` to understand the method signatures and return types.
- Look at `tests/conftest.py` for the `tmp_db_path` fixture pattern.
- Look at `tests/test_schema.py` for existing DB test patterns.
- Add a `Database` fixture in `conftest.py` that initializes the DB and returns a `Database()` instance with the temp path.

title: Add tests for FileManager (app/storage/files.py)
body:
## Summary

The `FileManager` class in `app/storage/files.py` handles all file I/O for the project — saving transcripts, summaries, reports, and uploaded files. It's 47 lines with 7 public methods, but has zero tests.

## Scope

- Write a test suite in `tests/test_files.py`.
- Use `pytest`'s built-in `tmp_path` fixture for a temporary directory.
- Test all public methods:
  - `save_upload` — writes a binary stream to the `raw/` subdirectory
  - `save_transcript` — writes text under `transcripts/<source_id>/transcript.txt`
  - `save_summary` — writes text under `summaries/<source_id>/summary.md`
  - `save_report` — writes content to `reports/` with the correct extension (both str and bytes)
  - `clean_temp` — removes files from `temp/` subdirectory
- Also test edge cases: long filenames (safe_filename truncation), empty strings, deeply nested source IDs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All public methods are tested
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_files.py -v` passes
- [ ] No files are left behind after tests (use `tmp_path` auto-cleanup)
- [ ] Tests verify both file content and file existence

## Getting Started

- Read `app/storage/files.py` and `app/utils/helpers.py` (for `safe_filename`).
- Use `pytest`'s `tmp_path` fixture as the data_dir.
- Use `io.BytesIO` to simulate file uploads for `save_upload`.

title: Add tests for YouTube ingestion (app/ingestion/youtube.py)
body:
## Summary

The `app/ingestion/youtube.py` module (144 lines) handles three operations: fetching YouTube captions via `youtube-transcript-api`, downloading audio via `yt-dlp`, and extracting video metadata. It's a critical pipeline component with no tests.

## Scope

- Write a test suite in `tests/test_youtube_ingestion.py`.
- Use `unittest.mock` (or `pytest-mock`) to mock:
  - `youtube_transcript_api.YouTubeTranscriptApi.fetch()` — for `get_captions()`
  - `subprocess.run` — for `download_audio()` and `extract_metadata()`
  - Filesystem operations — for output directory creation
- Test at minimum:
  - `get_captions(url)` — returns correct dict structure when captions found
  - `get_captions(url)` — returns `None` when captions unavailable/disabled (mock exceptions from youtube_transcript_api)
  - `extract_metadata(url)` — returns parsed JSON from yt-dlp
  - `download_audio(url, output_dir)` — returns correct result dict with title, audio_path, metadata
  - `_extract_video_id(url)` — handles all 3 URL patterns (v=, youtu.be/, embed/)
  - `_extract_video_id(url)` — returns None for invalid URLs
  - `_build_cmd()` — adds cookies file when it exists

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All public functions (`get_captions`, `extract_metadata`, `download_audio`) are tested
- [ ] `_extract_video_id` is tested with multiple URL patterns
- [ ] Mock uses are appropriate — no real API/network calls
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_youtube_ingestion.py -v` passes

## Getting Started

- Read `app/ingestion/youtube.py` in full.
- Use `mocker.patch('subprocess.run')` to mock subprocess calls.
- Look at how `YouTubeTranscriptApi` exceptions are caught (e.g., `TranscriptsDisabled`, `NoTranscriptFound`).
- Edge case: cookies file at `data/cookies.txt` affects `_build_cmd()` output.

title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow
body:
## Summary

SignalForge has 27 pytest tests but no CI pipeline. Adding a GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run tests on every push and pull request, helping maintain quality as the project grows.

## Scope

- Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with a basic CI workflow.
- It should:
  - Trigger on `push` and `pull_request` to `main`
  - Run on `ubuntu-latest`
  - Set up Python 3.12
  - Install dependencies from `requirements.txt`
  - Run `pytest tests/ -v`
  - (Optional) Add a lint step with `pip install ruff` and `ruff check .`
- Pin a `requirements-dev.txt` (or add `pytest`, `pytest-mock`, `ruff` to a dev extras) so CI doesn't install unnecessary packages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists and is valid YAML
- [ ] Workflow definition follows GitHub Actions best practices
- [ ] Tests run in the CI environment (all 27+ existing pass)
- [ ] CI badge can be added to `README.md` (optional but nice)

## Getting Started

- Look at GitHub's [Python CI starter workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-python).
- The project has `pytest`, `pytest-mock` in `requirements.txt` — those will install in CI.
- Consider adding a `requirements-dev.txt` with `ruff>=0.5.0` for optional linting.
- Test the workflow by pushing to a branch and checking Actions tab.

title: Add tests for Markdown report generation (app/reports/md_gen.py)
body:
## Summary

The `app/reports/md_gen.py` module (123 lines) contains a pure function `generate_markdown()` that produces the weekly intelligence report as a Markdown string. It's a pure function — no I/O, no side effects — making it ideal for comprehensive, beginner-friendly testing.

## Scope

- Write a test suite in `tests/test_md_gen.py`.
- Test `generate_markdown()` with various input configurations:
  - Minimal arguments (required only)
  - All sections populated (insights, action_items, quotes, themes, etc.)
  - Empty lists for optional sections (ensure no errors and no empty sections in output)
  - Single items vs multiple items in list fields
  - `report_sections` dict with all 4 keys (`key_developments`, `cross_source_connections`, `recommended_actions`, `signals_to_monitor`)
  - `sources` list with dict items (verify URL rendering)
  - Edge case: extremely long strings (verify no crash)
- Verify output structure using string assertions:
  - Title `#` header is present
  - Week and source count metadata are present
  - Section headers (`## Executive Summary`, `## Key Insights`, etc.) appear only when corresponding data is non-empty
  - Bullet points and numbered lists format correctly
  - Opportunities with `dict` items render `**title**` and `*Why:*` correctly

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `generate_markdown()` is tested with at least 8 distinct input configurations
- [ ] Required fields always render; empty optional fields produce no section header
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_md_gen.py -v` passes
- [ ] No mocking needed — pure function testing only

## Getting Started

- Read `app/reports/md_gen.py` to understand all parameters and return format.
- Look at `tests/test_chunker.py` for simple pure-function test patterns.
- Use `pytest.mark.parametrize` for testing multiple input combinations efficiently.

title: Add input validation and error categorization in bot.py Telegram handlers
body:
## Summary

The main bot module `bot.py` (535 lines) has several Telegram command handlers that use broad `except Exception` blocks with generic "Something went wrong" error messages. This makes debugging difficult for users and developers alike.

## Scope

- Improve error handling in these handlers: `ingest_youtube`, `ingest_text_cmd`, `handle_file`, `report`
- For each handler, categorize expected errors and provide specific user-facing messages:
  - Network/API errors (timeouts, rate limits) → "⚠️ Service temporarily unavailable, try again later."
  - Invalid input (bad URL, unsupported file format) → clear explanation of what's wrong
  - Processing errors (transcription failed, extraction failed) → specific failure reason
  - Unexpected errors → fallback generic message but include a reference code or log hint
- Add input validation:
  - Validate YouTube URLs more strictly before attempting processing
  - Validate file extensions in `handle_file` before downloading
  - Validate source IDs in `summary_cmd` (existing check is good, add bounds check)
- Use `logging` more granularly (include handler name, source_id if available)
- Write unit tests for the validation helper functions in `tests/test_bot_validation.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each handler has at least 3 distinct error paths with specific user messages
- [ ] YouTube URL validation is stricter (reject non-YouTube URLs early)
- [ ] File type validation happens before download (reject .exe, .zip, etc.)
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -v` continues to pass
- [ ] Log messages include handler context for debugging

## Getting Started

- Read `bot.py` to understand the error handling pattern in each handler.
- Look at the existing `_YOUTUBE_RE` regex on line 479 — consider making it more robust.
- Edge case: `handle_file` accesses `update.message.document` or `update.message.audio` or `update.message.voice` without checking which one is non-None.
